title: Add and subtract fractions with like denominators and write the answer in lowest terms (5/8 + 7/8 = 1 1/2)

lesson.title: Adding Fractions with the Same Bottom Number

steps.say: You already know how to simplify a fraction and how to turn an improper fraction into a mixed number. Today we use both of those on one small job: adding and subtracting fractions when the bottom numbers already match.

Think of a granola bar scored into eight equal pieces. The bottom number, the denominator, tells you the size of each piece — eighths. The top number just counts how many of those pieces you have. So when the pieces are already the same size, you only count them up. Five eighths plus seven eighths means five pieces plus seven pieces.

visual.caption: Five eighths and seven eighths — same size pieces, ready to combine

steps.say: Five plus seven is twelve, and the pieces are still eighths, so we get twelve eighths. That is more than one whole bar, which is totally fine — an improper fraction is just an honest answer that we are not finished tidying up yet.

visual.caption: Twelve eighths — one full bar plus four more eighths

steps.say: Now finish it in lowest terms. Twelve and eight both divide by four, so twelve eighths becomes three halves, and three halves is one and one half. Subtracting works exactly the same way: nine twelfths minus three twelfths is six twelfths, which tidies up to one half.

visual.caption: Three halves — the same amount, said in the simplest way

steps.say: Two traps to dodge. First, never add the bottom numbers: one quarter plus one quarter is two quarters, which is one half — it is not two eighths, because your pieces did not shrink when you added them. Second, do not stop early: twelve sixteenths is not done at six eighths, because six and eight still share a factor of two, so keep going to three quarters.

visual.caption: One quarter added to one quarter fills two quarters — the pieces stay quarters

steps.say: So the whole move is: same bottom number, add or subtract the tops, then simplify and change to a mixed number if it is bigger than one.

lesson.answer: Same denominator: add or subtract the numerators only, keep the denominator, then simplify to lowest terms.

practice.question: Picture your monthly phone data as one bar split into twelve equal parts. In the first week you used five twelfths of it, and in the second week you used another three twelfths. Draw the bar if it helps. How much data have you used in total, written in lowest terms?
practice.answer: Five twelfths plus three twelfths is eight twelfths. Both eight and twelve divide by four, so the answer in lowest terms is two thirds of your data.
